build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The tug uses inertia-based movement with visible acceleration and coasting; thrusters fire in response to player input and the ship drifts when thrust stops. Score 0 if the ship is static or instantly jumps to positions.

A tractor beam attaches to salvage and visibly links the tug to the object while towing it over multiple frames; the beam stretches or adjusts as the tug moves. Score 0 if pickup is only a counter change or the beam is decorative and does not affect motion.

Salvage mass or type visibly affects tug handling, tow speed, or fuel consumption while towing. Heavier pieces drag the ship differently than lighter ones. Score 0 if all salvage pieces behave identically when towed.

Hazards such as gravity wells, mines, radiation arcs, or debris storms visibly threaten or redirect the player, with warning feedback before or during danger. Score 0 if hazards are absent or purely decorative.

Fuel, heat, or energy depletes during thrust and constrains how aggressively the player can maneuver; running low has observable consequences such as reduced thrust or mission failure. Score 0 if fuel is absent or infinite.

Delivering salvage to a station or recovery zone awards credits, completes contract progress, or changes mission status visibly. The delivery loop is functional end to end. Score 0 if delivery has no state change or reward.

At least three distinct salvage or contract types are visible with different value, risk, mass, or visual identity such as light panels, heavy cores, volatile capsules, or black boxes. Score 0 if there is only one generic salvage object.

Mission pressure escalates through fuel limits, contract timers, damage accumulation, richer salvage in harder locations, or later phases with tougher routing. The player faces increasing challenge over time. Score 0 if the scene remains a single unchanging pickup with no escalation.

An upgrade or planning screen offers choices such as thrust power, beam strength, hull plating, or fuel capacity, and choosing one visibly changes later play. Score 0 if there is no upgrade or reinvestment layer.

Victory and failure result screens show credits earned, fuel spent, salvage delivered, damage taken, and retry/title controls. Results reflect prior mission performance. Score 0 if results are missing.

A styled title screen shows the game name, a clear Start or Contract control, and space-salvage imagery such as a tug, debris, station, or starfield. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI with no theme.

The flow connects title or scenario -> contract selection -> salvage field play -> delivery or failure -> result/retry/title navigation without restarting the executable. Score 0 if major transitions are missing.

The HUD clearly shows fuel or heat, velocity or thrust state, active contract, salvage value or mass, credits, delivery target indicator, and hazard warnings in readable non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if the player cannot tell what to tow or where to deliver.

Readability at 1280x720 is strong: tug, salvage, beam, hazards, station, HUD elements, and contract info are distinguishable and do not overlap or become ambiguous. Score 0 if navigation or mission state is unreadable.

Art direction is coherent across title, tug, salvage, tractor beam, station, hazards, HUD, contracts, upgrades, and result screens. A consistent palette, typography, iconography, spacing, and visual hierarchy hold the game together at a publishable vertical-slice standard. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

The space environment uses real sprite or procedural art for the starfield, asteroids, station, debris, and hazard zones — not plain ColorRect fills or default HTML 引擎 primitives. Different field elements are visually distinct and recognisable. Score 0 if the environment is uniform color fills or unstyled rectangles.

HUD and UI chrome: fuel gauges, contract panels, delivery indicators, upgrade menus, and result screens use styled themed widgets (custom panels, icon buttons, illustrated frames, or themed StyleBox), not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Numeric text uses a custom or styled font. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled default default widgets or if chrome treatments differ wildly between screens.

Animation and feedback make space salvage legible: thrusters flare on input, the beam stretches or glows while towing, salvage trails behind, hazards pulse warnings, delivery rewards animate, and state changes use tween or particles rather than instant snaps. Score 0 if all changes snap silently with no animation.
